The Sokoto State Government has reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening security partnerships, promoting defence innovation and adopting modern technologies to tackle security challenges in the state and the wider North-West region. The Governor’s Special Adviser on Security Matters, Col. Ahmed Usman (retd.), stated this while representing Governor Ahmed Aliyu at the opening ceremony of the Africa International Defence Exhibition 2026, held at Eko Atlantic, Lagos. Usman, in a statement made available to journalists in Sokoto on Tuesday, described the exhibition as an important platform for strengthening Africa’s collective security architecture through technological innovation, local defence production and strategic cooperation. He said the growing threats of terrorism, banditry, transnational organised crime and other emerging security challenges required stronger collaboration among governments, security agencies, defence manufacturers and technology providers. According to him, African countries must invest more in indigenous research, local manufacturing and technological advancement to develop sustainable solutions to their security challenges. The security adviser stressed that effective security management went beyond deploying security personnel and military hardware, noting that intelligence gathering, surveillance, modern communication systems, capacity building and inter-agency cooperation were equally important. He said the Sokoto State Government recognised the importance of strategic partnerships and modern security solutions in addressing the security challenges confronting the state and the North-West region. He expressed optimism that AFRIDEX 2026 would provide opportunities for meaningful partnerships between Nigeria’s defence industry and international technology providers, particularly in intelligence gathering, equipment manufacturing, border surveillance and unmanned systems. He also commended the Defence Industries Corporation of Nigeria for organising the exhibition, describing it as a significant step towards positioning Nigeria as a major contributor to Africa’s defence and security industry. The exhibition was officially declared open on behalf of President Bola Tinubu by the President of the Senate, who attended as the Special Guest of Honour. The ceremony attracted top government officials and security stakeholders, including the Chief of Defence Staff, service chiefs, ministers of defence, senior military officers, general officers commanding, flag officers commanding, air officers commanding and the President of the ECOWAS Commission. AFRIDEX 2026, held from October 26 to 29 at Eko Atlantic, Lagos, brought together local and international stakeholders to showcase defence technologies, promote indigenous industrial capacity and strengthen cooperation among African countries and international partners. The Sokoto State Government reiterated its readiness to embrace innovative security solutions and strategic partnerships to promote lasting peace, stability and sustainable development.
